params.body:
Vera's first real publish from its own machine was refused by the gateway with `http: request body too large`. The armed review page of the ProveML paper is 8.4 MB of HTML, 11.2 MB once it travels as base64 inside the submission, and the limit was 8 MiB, a number chosen when the only large submission was a branch.push with its lockfiles.

- The limit stays, because it is what keeps whoever reaches the port from filling a sealed machine. It is now 32 MiB, which fits the work the hands actually do.
- A body over it is refused as 413 with "the submission is larger than 32 MiB". Go reports it as a read error, so without naming it a hand cannot tell "too large" from "connection lost" and retries what will never fit. That is how this cost half an hour tonight.
- The test pins both: over the limit refused by name, within the limit judged on its shape.

After this: a tag, the sha256 in `deploy/gcp/startup.sh`, `rehearse.sh upgrade`.
params.title: Een inzending mag wegen wat het werk weegt
